coverage: A curated review of all previously included programs, with selected important additions. It is not an exhaustive registry of every ALS study worldwide.
methodology: Evidence cutoff: 10 September 2026. Sources were retrieved on 11 September 2026; dated developments after the cutoff are excluded.
Regulators establish approved indications. Trial registries establish the recorded design, phase and recruitment status. Registry dates are shown because records can lag behind events.
Published controlled results take precedence over subgroup claims. Sponsor announcements are labeled and used for operational milestones or explicitly preliminary findings.
Undated manufacturer pages describe product capabilities only; they do not establish a dated approval or verified availability on the cutoff date.
A biomarker measures a biological process. A change in NfL, TDP-43 or another marker is not automatically a demonstrated clinical benefit.
No medical specialist sign-off is claimed. Treatment suitability, genetic findings, access and current recruitment should be confirmed with the relevant clinical team.

approved_treatments.name: Riluzole
approved_treatments.subtitle: Rilutek · oral formulations
approved_treatments.summary: An oral treatment with randomized evidence of a modest survival benefit in ALS.
approved_treatments.evidence: The pivotal trial studied 959 people. A Cochrane synthesis estimated roughly two to three months of median survival benefit in the trial populations; that average is not a prediction for an individual.
limitations: It does not regenerate motor neurons. Treatment choice, formulation and monitoring belong in a discussion with the treating neurologist.
approved_treatments.india_note: Ask the prescribing team and a licensed pharmacy about the appropriate formulation, current supply and a written price quotation.

approved_treatments.name: Edaravone
approved_treatments.subtitle: Radicava · Radicava ORS
approved_treatments.summary: Edaravone is approved in the US for ALS. The oral suspension provides an alternative to intravenous administration and can also be given through a feeding tube.
approved_treatments.evidence: FDA describes evidence of less decline in daily functioning in a six-month trial. Oral approval used comparable drug exposure to the IV product. This supports slowing decline in the studied population, not recovery of lost function.
limitations: Limited evidence in a particular disease stage does not prove that every person outside the trial criteria cannot benefit. Avoid blanket exclusions based on wheelchair or ventilator use.
approved_treatments.india_note: Verify the exact product and route locally. US approval of Radicava ORS does not establish its routine availability in India.

approved_treatments.name: Tofersen
approved_treatments.subtitle: Qalsody · SOD1-targeted antisense therapy
approved_treatments.summary: Approved for adults with ALS and a SOD1 mutation. The FDA decision was based on lowering blood neurofilament light (NfL), a marker of nerve injury.
approved_treatments.evidence: The 28-week VALOR trial did not establish a significant primary clinical benefit. Longer follow-up associated earlier treatment with less decline, but the open-label comparison has limitations. Clinical benefit remains under confirmatory study.
limitations: A biomarker response is not proof of a cure or predictable recovery. Intrathecal treatment requires a specialist team. Investigation in non-SOD1 ALS does not expand the approved indication.
approved_treatments.india_note: Confirm the genetic result with a specialist. Local authorization, supply, import permission and funding must be checked for the individual patient.

approved_treatments.name: High-dose mecobalamin
approved_treatments.subtitle: Rozebalamin · development code E0302
approved_treatments.summary: Japan approved this injectable methylcobalamin formulation for slowing functional impairment in ALS. It is distinct from routine vitamin B12 supplementation.
approved_treatments.evidence: JETALS found less ALSFRS-R decline over 16 weeks in a selected early-stage Japanese population. The PMDA review supports the indication while documenting the studied population and safety requirements.
limitations: Do not generalize the short trial to all stages or substitute ordinary supplements. Rozebalamin is mecobalamin (E0302), not MT-1186.
approved_treatments.india_note: Japanese authorization does not mean approval or reliable supply in India. Discuss product identity and any lawful access route with the clinical team.

symptom_management.name: Dextromethorphan / quinidine
symptom_management.subtitle: Nuedexta · pseudobulbar affect
symptom_management.summary: US-approved for pseudobulbar affect: episodes of involuntary laughing or crying that can occur in neurological conditions, including ALS.
symptom_management.evidence: The FDA indication addresses pseudobulbar affect. It is not an approval for slowing ALS progression or extending survival.
limitations: Suitability and interactions need a prescribing clinician. Symptom benefit should not be counted as disease modification.
symptom_management.india_note: Local availability and alternatives should be discussed with the neurologist; no current Indian price or supply guarantee is established here.

clinical_trials.name: TRCN-1023
clinical_trials.subtitle: FUNCtion ALS · UNC13A restoration
clinical_trials.summary: A new Phase 1/2 study evaluates a medicine intended to restore UNC13A function in ALS.
clinical_trials.evidence: The registry was updated on 9 September 2026. It describes a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled trial assessing safety, tolerability and early signals after intrathecal administration.
limitations: No results are posted. A newly recruiting trial is an opportunity to test a hypothesis, not evidence of clinical benefit.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: Pridopidine
clinical_trials.subtitle: PREVAiLS · sigma-1 receptor agonist
clinical_trials.summary: The Phase 3 PREVAiLS study tests pridopidine in people with early, rapidly progressive ALS.
clinical_trials.evidence: First enrollment was announced on 30 March 2026; the registry still lists recruiting. The earlier HEALEY trial did not meet its primary endpoint. Subgroup observations motivated a more focused confirmatory trial.
limitations: Subgroup findings are hypothesis-generating. PREVAiLS has not yet established efficacy or supported ALS marketing approval.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: CNM-Au8
clinical_trials.subtitle: Clene · gold nanocrystal suspension
clinical_trials.summary: An investigational therapy targeting cellular energy pathways; CNM-Au8 remains under development for ALS.
clinical_trials.evidence: Clene’s 14 August update targets an accelerated-approval application in early Q4 2026. Its HEALEY trial did not show significant benefit on the primary 24-week progression endpoint. Later biomarker and survival analyses underpin the planned submission.
limitations: A planned application, FDA meeting or exploratory analysis is not approval. RESTORE-ALS should not be described as enrolling without a verified launch.
clinical_trials.india_note: No routine Indian access or local trial site is established by these sources. Expanded access is distinct from marketing approval.

clinical_trials.name: NurOwn / debamestrocel
clinical_trials.subtitle: ENDURANCE · autologous cell therapy
clinical_trials.summary: ENDURANCE is the planned confirmatory study of cells prepared from a participant’s own bone marrow.
clinical_trials.evidence: The August 2026 sponsor update describes preparations to open the study; the registry lists not yet recruiting. An FDA-agreed Special Protocol Assessment concerns trial design and does not establish that the treatment works.
limitations: The new trial has no posted results. Do not present NurOwn as an approved stem-cell treatment or imply that protocol agreement guarantees approval.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: Masitinib
clinical_trials.subtitle: AB23005 · add-on to standard care
clinical_trials.summary: A confirmatory Phase 3 study is registered for this investigational kinase inhibitor.
clinical_trials.evidence: The registry lists not yet recruiting. In April 2026 AB Science described the ALS study as not yet started and a temporary European trial halt. EMA’s earlier refusal cited unreliable study data and insufficiently demonstrated benefit.
limitations: Post-hoc or preprint survival analyses do not overturn the regulatory refusal or establish an approved treatment.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: Ulefnersen / ION363
clinical_trials.subtitle: FUSION · FUS-targeted antisense therapy
clinical_trials.summary: A Phase 3 trial in ALS associated with pathogenic FUS mutations.
clinical_trials.evidence: The July 2026 registry lists active follow-up with enrollment closed and no results posted. The study evaluates efficacy and safety of lowering FUS protein.
limitations: This genetically defined program cannot be generalized to all ALS. An anticipated readout is not a completed positive result.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: QRL-201
clinical_trials.subtitle: ANQUR · STMN2 restoration
clinical_trials.summary: An antisense approach intended to restore stathmin-2 expression affected by TDP-43 dysfunction.
clinical_trials.evidence: QurAlis reported interim target-engagement and biomarker findings in February 2026, with an overall trend and subgroup signals in function. The sponsor calls ANQUR Phase 1/2; the registry classifies it Phase 1 and lists enrollment closed.
limitations: Interim and subgroup results are not confirmatory efficacy. A proposed 2027 Phase 3 program remains a plan.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: PrimeC
clinical_trials.subtitle: NeuroSense · extended-release combination
clinical_trials.summary: An investigational fixed-dose formulation of ciprofloxacin and celecoxib.
clinical_trials.evidence: On 31 August 2026 NeuroSense announced plans to optimize PARAGON into a smaller, shorter pivotal study, subject to FDA alignment. A Canadian submission is targeted for December 2026. Neither milestone should be described as completed.
limitations: Earlier clinical and biomarker signals require confirmation. The formulation is not interchangeable with self-combining its component medicines.
clinical_trials.india_note: An Indian approval, launch date or price is not established by this development announcement.

clinical_trials.name: COYA 302
clinical_trials.subtitle: ALSTARS · immune regulation
clinical_trials.summary: A combination biologic strategy intended to enhance regulatory T-cell activity.
clinical_trials.evidence: The August update reports continuing enrollment and targets topline data in Q1 2027. The sponsor describes ALSTARS as Phase 2; ClinicalTrials.gov lists Phase 2/3. Both descriptions refer to the same study.
limitations: No randomized efficacy results are posted. Trial phase and Fast Track designation are not evidence of approval.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: NUZ-001
clinical_trials.subtitle: HEALEY Regimen I · S-monepantel
clinical_trials.summary: An investigational oral medicine designed to support clearance of harmful cellular proteins.
clinical_trials.evidence: The HEALEY trial center reports enrollment complete, consistent with the July 2026 registry status. The Phase 2/3 cohort is now in follow-up; no efficacy results are posted.
limitations: Small earlier safety studies and open-label observations do not establish slowing of ALS progression.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: SPG302 / tazbentatol
clinical_trials.subtitle: Spinogenix · synaptic function
clinical_trials.summary: A small molecule being studied for effects on synaptic function; clinical benefit in ALS remains unconfirmed.
clinical_trials.evidence: The early study is registered as completed. The sponsor reported Phase 2a findings in November 2025. A separate US expanded-access protocol is listed as available (NCT07088159).
limitations: Early functional observations and access outside a trial do not prove synapse regeneration or reliable functional recovery in people with ALS.
clinical_trials.india_note: The US expanded-access protocol is not an Indian approval or a guarantee that an overseas patient can join.

clinical_trials.name: ATLX-1282
clinical_trials.subtitle: Alchemab / Lilly · antibody program
clinical_trials.summary: A therapeutic antibody program derived from research into biological resilience.
clinical_trials.evidence: Alchemab announced a first-in-human Phase 1 trial on 9 September 2025. The program was licensed to Lilly. No later ALS efficacy result was established in this review.
limitations: A licensing agreement does not validate efficacy. Current patient recruitment and a Phase 2 start date have not been verified.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian trial site or commercial access is verified. Corporate presence in India does not establish future access.

clinical_trials.name: NX210c
clinical_trials.subtitle: SEALS · neuroprotective peptide
clinical_trials.summary: A Phase 2 study of an intravenous peptide approach to neuroprotection and blood–brain barrier function.
clinical_trials.evidence: June 2026 preliminary results cover 82 randomized participants. Axoltis reported exploratory functional and biomarker trends; the cited early NfL comparison was not statistically significant.
limitations: Preliminary conference findings need the full controlled analysis. Biomarker trends must not be presented as proven survival benefit.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: XS-228 / XS228CN
clinical_trials.subtitle: XellSmart · iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells
clinical_trials.summary: A Phase 1 ALS study in China evaluates induced-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived motor neuron progenitor cells.
clinical_trials.evidence: The ALS-specific record NCT07118319 lists recruiting and no posted results. Separate XS228 spinal-cord-injury trials must not be used as evidence of benefit in ALS.
limitations: Safety, integration of transplanted cells and clinical benefit remain experimental. There is no established restoration of lost motor neurons or function.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: AMX0114
clinical_trials.subtitle: LUMINA · calpain-2 antisense therapy
clinical_trials.summary: A Phase 1 study of an antisense medicine targeting calpain-2.
clinical_trials.evidence: Amylyx’s June 2026 update reported no drug-related serious adverse events in the lowest-dose cohort, while the measured biomarkers remained near baseline. Higher-dose cohorts are being evaluated.
limitations: Tolerability at a low dose is not evidence of clinical efficacy. Dose-escalation findings are still early.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: NB-4746
clinical_trials.subtitle: Nura Bio · SARM1 inhibitor
clinical_trials.summary: SARM1 inhibition has now entered ALS patient testing with this oral investigational drug.
clinical_trials.evidence: Nura Bio announced the first ALS participant dosed in June 2026. The Phase 1b/2a program measures safety, drug exposure and biomarkers; registry sites are in Australia and Canada.
limitations: The biological rationale and healthy-volunteer findings do not yet demonstrate benefit in ALS. This program is distinct from preclinical ASHA-624.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: CTx1000
clinical_trials.subtitle: KOANEWA · TDP-43-directed gene therapy
clinical_trials.summary: An early gene-therapy study intended to clear pathological TDP-43.
clinical_trials.evidence: Celosia announced first dosing in March 2026 at Macquarie University Hospital. The Phase 1b study is open-label and focuses on safety and tolerability. The recruiting registry record was last updated in February.
limitations: The registry is older than the dosing announcement: confirm current enrollment directly. Reversal in animal models is not evidence of reversal in people.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: RAG-17
clinical_trials.subtitle: SOD1-targeted siRNA
clinical_trials.summary: A July 2026 Nature Medicine paper reports early human testing of an RNA-silencing approach for SOD1 ALS.
clinical_trials.evidence: The published first study involved six participants and examined safety, exposure and preliminary biological or clinical observations. A separate Phase 1 trial is registered as recruiting.
limitations: Six participants without a definitive controlled efficacy comparison cannot establish survival benefit or superiority to tofersen. Enrollment status needs confirmation because the cited registry update is older.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: Usnoflast
clinical_trials.subtitle: UNITE-ALS · Zydus
clinical_trials.summary: A Phase 2b randomized study of an oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor.
clinical_trials.evidence: The 1 September 2026 registry update lists recruiting, with multiple countries participating and no results posted. This is an investigational ALS program associated with an Indian-origin sponsor.
limitations: Sponsor origin does not mean a trial is taking place in India or that the medicine is approved there.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: ALN-SOD
clinical_trials.subtitle: SOD1-targeted RNA interference
clinical_trials.summary: A first-in-human Phase 1/2 study for adults with a SOD1 mutation.
clinical_trials.evidence: The July 2026 registry lists ongoing recruitment and evaluates safety and pharmacological effects of an RNA-interference approach.
limitations: No results are posted. This is a separate investigational product from approved tofersen and from RAG-17.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: VTx-002
clinical_trials.subtitle: PIONEER-ALS · gene therapy
clinical_trials.summary: A first-in-human Phase 1/2 program using a vectorized antibody approach directed at TDP-43 pathology.
clinical_trials.evidence: The registry updated on 10 September 2026 lists recruiting at sites in Europe and the US. It is an open-label ascending-dose study with clinical and biomarker assessments.
limitations: No results are posted. Small uncontrolled gene-therapy studies establish early safety information, not a proven ALS treatment. The older sponsor mechanism page still says preclinical; use the dated registry for current trial status.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: INS1202
clinical_trials.subtitle: Insmed · investigational genetic therapy
clinical_trials.summary: A single-dose Phase 1 study in adults with SOD1 ALS or ALS without a known ALS-related genetic mutation.
clinical_trials.evidence: The September 2026 registry lists recruiting in the US. The study evaluates safety, tolerability and pharmacodynamic effects after intrathecal administration.
limitations: There are no posted efficacy results. Eligibility is protocol-specific and must be confirmed by the study team.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: Tofersen in non-SOD1 ALS
clinical_trials.subtitle: Investigator-led Phase 2 study
clinical_trials.summary: An exploratory trial tests whether tofersen has biological or clinical effects beyond genetically confirmed SOD1 ALS.
clinical_trials.evidence: The registry updated in June 2026 lists a US Phase 2 study and excludes SOD1- and FUS-associated disease. This is a research question with no posted results.
limitations: The FDA-approved indication remains SOD1 ALS. This trial is not evidence to prescribe tofersen broadly for sporadic ALS.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: Dazucorilant
clinical_trials.subtitle: DAZALS · glucocorticoid receptor modulation
clinical_trials.summary: DAZALS missed its primary functional endpoint. Corcept is pursuing further study after secondary and exploratory survival findings.
clinical_trials.evidence: The April 2026 sponsor report describes two-year survival analyses and a planned Phase 3 trial. The long-term comparisons include selected participants who did or did not enter the extension. The registry still says recruiting, which should not be read as enrollment in the planned pivotal study.
limitations: Survival signals after a failed primary endpoint need confirmation, especially with selection into an extension. No results posted in a registry does not mean results have not been reported elsewhere. Confirm any enrollment directly.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

clinical_trials.name: LTX-002
clinical_trials.subtitle: NeurALS · SPTLC1-targeted antisense therapy
clinical_trials.summary: A new Phase 1/2 study investigates an RNA-targeted approach to abnormal lipid metabolism in ALS.
clinical_trials.evidence: Leal announced first dosing in June 2026. The August registry lists a blinded, placebo-controlled dose-escalation study assessing safety, tolerability and pharmacological effects.
limitations: The rationale extends to sporadic and genetic ALS, but clinical benefit has not been established. This is a first-in-human program with no posted results.
clinical_trials.india_note: No Indian site is listed in the cited record. Recruitment elsewhere does not guarantee eligibility, travel support or access from India.

preclinical_research.name: ASHA-624 and axon protection
preclinical_research.subtitle: SARM1 biology
preclinical_research.summary: ASHA-624 is a molecular-glue strategy designed to hold SARM1 inactive and protect axons.
preclinical_research.evidence: The identified funder announcement supports preclinical studies in an inherited optic-nerve disease. It does not establish an ALS clinical trial or human ALS efficacy.
limitations: Do not equate promising work in another disease model with an available ALS therapy. NB-4746 is the distinct SARM1 program now in ALS clinical testing.
preclinical_research.india_note: Research only; no verified clinical access for ASHA-624.

preclinical_research.name: RNA-targeting CRISPR
preclinical_research.subtitle: C9ORF72-linked ALS / FTD
preclinical_research.summary: Researchers are investigating precise removal of disease-associated repeat RNA while preserving normal gene activity.
preclinical_research.evidence: A 2025 Nature Communications study used a high-fidelity Cas13 system in experimental models of C9ORF72-linked disease and reduced molecular abnormalities.
limitations: This is laboratory and animal-model evidence. Delivery, off-target effects and long-term safety need evaluation before claims of human benefit.
preclinical_research.india_note: No approved CRISPR treatment for ALS is established by this study.

preclinical_research.name: Blocking toxic repeat translation
preclinical_research.subtitle: C9ORF72-linked ALS / FTD
preclinical_research.summary: A 2026 study separates the toxicity of repeat-derived proteins from the effects of the repeat RNA itself.
preclinical_research.evidence: The Science paper reports rescue of disease-related phenotypes in models by blocking repeat-associated translation without removing the repeat RNA.
limitations: Mechanistic advances can identify future targets, but do not demonstrate an effective medicine in patients.
preclinical_research.india_note: A research finding, not a clinical treatment or enrollment offer.

preclinical_research.name: TDP-43 condensate modulation
preclinical_research.subtitle: Dewpoint Therapeutics
preclinical_research.summary: Small molecules are being developed to correct abnormal TDP-43 condensates and restore RNA-processing functions.
preclinical_research.evidence: Dewpoint selected a development candidate in January 2026 on the basis of cell and animal-model findings.
limitations: A development candidate is not a tested or approved ALS treatment. No human efficacy result is established in the cited announcement.
preclinical_research.india_note: No clinical access is established by the cited preclinical program.

withdrawn_treatments.name: Relyvrio / Albrioza
withdrawn_treatments.subtitle: AMX0035 · sodium phenylbutyrate / taurursodiol
withdrawn_treatments.summary: The medicine was removed from the US and Canadian markets after its confirmatory trial failed.
withdrawn_treatments.evidence: Amylyx announced withdrawal in April 2024 following PHOENIX, which did not meet its prespecified primary and secondary endpoints.
limitations: Earlier approval and positive small-study results do not outweigh a failed confirmatory trial. Current care should be discussed with the treating clinician.
withdrawn_treatments.india_note: Do not present this as a currently marketed ALS treatment or recommend purchasing a substitute combination.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: Fosigotifator
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: ABBV-CLS-7262 · HEALEY Regimen F
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: The tested eIF2B activator did not establish efficacy in the HEALEY study.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: Calico reported in January 2025 that neither the primary nor exploratory higher dose met the primary endpoint. Key secondary endpoints for the primary dose also were not significantly different from placebo.
limitations: Exploratory findings cannot be presented as an approved benefit. A negative trial does not, by itself, prove every future study of the mechanism must fail.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: DNL343
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: HEALEY Regimen G · eIF2B activation
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: DNL343 did not demonstrate slowing of ALS progression in the tested regimen.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: The January 2025 announcement reports that the primary combined function/survival endpoint and key strength and respiratory secondary endpoints were not met at 24 weeks.
limitations: Safety or a biological rationale cannot substitute for a demonstrated clinical effect.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: BIIB105 / ION541
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: ALSpire · ataxin-2 antisense therapy
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: Biogen and Ionis ended development following the Phase 1/2 ALSpire study.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: The May 2024 announcement reports target lowering without evidence sufficient to support continued development for ALS.
limitations: Lowering a target protein alone does not establish that patients function better or live longer.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: SAR443820 / DNL788
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: HIMALAYA · RIPK1 inhibitor
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: The HIMALAYA Phase 2 program did not meet its ALS efficacy objective.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: The study registry records termination for lack of efficacy. This entry concerns the ALS study, not results from the separate multiple-sclerosis program.
limitations: Evidence from a different disease cannot be used to imply efficacy in ALS.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: Zilucoplan
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: HEALEY Regimen A · complement C5
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: The HEALEY trial stopped this regimen after a prespecified futility analysis.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: The published randomized study did not establish benefit on ALS progression.
limitations: Approval or benefit in another condition does not imply an ALS indication.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: Verdiperstat
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: HEALEY Regimen B · myeloperoxidase
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: The published randomized HEALEY study did not demonstrate slowing of ALS.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: Neither the prespecified primary endpoint nor the secondary endpoints differed significantly between active treatment and placebo.
limitations: This negative result belongs alongside other unsuccessful programs, rather than in a list of proven options.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: Trehalose
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: HEALEY Regimen E · autophagy
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: The intravenous trehalose regimen did not show evidence of slower ALS progression than placebo.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: The 2025 Lancet Neurology publication found no significant benefit in secondary clinical or biomarker measures either.
limitations: Laboratory effects on protein clearance do not establish clinical benefit, and oral supplements are not equivalent to the trial intervention.

failed_discontinued_trials.name: BIIB078
failed_discontinued_trials.subtitle: C9ORF72-targeted antisense therapy
failed_discontinued_trials.summary: Development ended after the Phase 1 randomized study in C9ORF72-associated ALS.
failed_discontinued_trials.evidence: The published trial found no reduction in neurofilament and no clinical benefit relative to placebo.
limitations: This result applies to this product and study; other approaches to C9ORF72 biology remain under investigation.

communication_technology.name: Tobii Dynavox AAC
communication_technology.subtitle: PCEye · TD I-Series · TD Pilot
communication_technology.summary: Dedicated eye-gaze and speech-generating products can provide communication and computer access as movement changes.
communication_technology.evidence: Manufacturer documentation distinguishes a computer eye tracker from integrated Windows and iPad-based speech devices. Selection depends on positioning, vision, fatigue and the person’s preferred communication system.
limitations: Product documentation describes capabilities, not a guarantee of individual performance. Assess with an AAC professional and trial the exact setup.
communication_technology.india_note: Request a local assessment and written quotation covering hardware, mount, software, warranty, repairs and language support.
communication_technology.what_it_is: Dedicated eye-gaze and speech-generating products can provide communication and computer access as movement changes.
communication_technology.how_it_works: Manufacturer documentation distinguishes a computer eye tracker from integrated Windows and iPad-based speech devices. Selection depends on positioning, vision, fatigue and the person’s preferred communication system.

india_availability.how_to_get: Request a local assessment and written quotation covering hardware, mount, software, warranty, repairs and language support.

communication_technology.realistic_expectations: Supports communication; it does not treat motor neuron degeneration.

communication_technology.name: EyeControl
communication_technology.subtitle: Wearable eye-tracking communication
communication_technology.summary: A wearable, screen-free approach uses eye movements with audio feedback to communicate needs.
communication_technology.evidence: An ALS feasibility study is registered, while current manufacturer documentation also describes a bedside hospital platform. Product configurations and clinical use cases must be distinguished.
limitations: A completed feasibility study does not guarantee reliable use for every person with advanced ALS. Verify the specific product and evidence with the supplier.

communication_technology.name: OptiKey with an eye tracker
communication_technology.subtitle: Open-source Windows communication software
communication_technology.summary: OptiKey supports typing, speech output and computer control using compatible input devices.
communication_technology.evidence: The maintainers explicitly removed support for Tobii Eye Tracker 5, EyeX and 4C in OptiKey 4. Legacy OptiKey 3.2.x supports these older use cases.
limitations: Do not assume the latest OptiKey works with the Tobii Eye Tracker 5 setup elsewhere in this project. Verify hardware, driver, Windows and application versions together.
communication_technology.india_note: Assess the existing hardware first. Budget for setup and assistance even where the software is free.

experimental_communication_tech.name: Pupil Labs Neon integrations
experimental_communication_tech.subtitle: Wearable gaze data · custom software
experimental_communication_tech.summary: Neon provides gaze and other eye signals for researchers and developers; it is not a complete ALS communication system.
experimental_communication_tech.evidence: The official real-time API can stream data to custom applications on the same network. That capability enables prototyping but does not establish clinical reliability for ALS.
limitations: Building a usable communication interface requires software, calibration/positioning work and individual testing. Do not equate raw gaze streaming with ready-to-use AAC.
experimental_communication_tech.india_note: Consider established AAC assessment first. A custom integration needs sustained technical support and a backup communication method.

experimental_communication_tech.name: Webcam head tracking
experimental_communication_tech.subtitle: Enable Viacam · alternative computer access
experimental_communication_tech.summary: Head-tracking software can move a cursor using movements observed by a webcam.
experimental_communication_tech.evidence: Enable Viacam’s documentation describes camera and tracking-area configuration. This is an access method for someone who can comfortably produce the required movements.
limitations: It is head tracking, not eye tracking. Weakness, fatigue and positioning can limit use; these tools are not established replacements for eye-gaze AAC.
experimental_communication_tech.india_note: Trial comfort and accuracy with an assistive-technology professional. Maintain a simple communication backup.

experimental_communication_tech.subtitle: Prototype concepts · including AprilTag setups
experimental_communication_tech.summary: Marker-based and smartphone experiments should be treated as engineering prototypes.
experimental_communication_tech.evidence: No ALS-specific clinical validation or supported complete communication product was established for the older page’s proposed DIY setup. The Pupil Labs API documentation supports only the general feasibility of custom data integrations.
limitations: Do not present a prototype, price estimate or working demo as reliable daily communication for a person with ALS.
experimental_communication_tech.india_note: Keep prototypes optional and supervised. They should not replace a dependable way to express urgent needs.

experimental_communication_tech.name: Brain-to-voice neuroprostheses
experimental_communication_tech.subtitle: Implanted brain–computer interfaces
experimental_communication_tech.summary: Research systems have enabled an individual with ALS to produce synthetic speech directly from recorded brain activity.
experimental_communication_tech.evidence: UC Davis reported real-time voice synthesis in June 2025 in a participant with ALS. This is a communication milestone rather than restoration of natural speech muscles.
limitations: Small participant numbers, implanted hardware and intensive specialist support limit generalization. These systems are not established routine home products.
experimental_communication_tech.india_note: Access is through formal research eligibility. Maintain practical AAC planning alongside interest in BCI research.

experimental_communication_tech.name: Connexus / Connect-One
experimental_communication_tech.subtitle: Paradromics · implanted BCI
experimental_communication_tech.summary: A 2026 early-feasibility study evaluates an implanted interface for communication and computer control.
experimental_communication_tech.evidence: The trial registry lists recruiting in the US and includes people with severe speech or movement impairment. Safety and device feasibility are central objectives.
limitations: A research authorization is not commercial approval. Surgery, long follow-up and strict eligibility distinguish this from buying an eye tracker.

india_research.name: ALS genetics in South Asia
india_research.subtitle: NIMHANS · India–UK collaboration
india_research.summary: India’s participation in a Target ALS-funded genome-wide association study broadens the ancestry represented in ALS genetics.
india_research.evidence: The funder describes an India–UK collaboration involving NIMHANS, with genetic analysis and longitudinal samples. This is research into disease risk and biology, not a treatment trial.
limitations: Research participation is not a guarantee of free clinical genetic testing, a diagnosis or access to a targeted medicine.
india_research.india_note: Ask the treating neurology center about genetic counseling, clinically appropriate testing and any currently open research protocol.

india_research.name: Longitudinal samples and natural history
india_research.subtitle: Target ALS · AIIMS New Delhi · NIMHANS
india_research.summary: Following participants over time can connect molecular changes with clinical progression.
india_research.evidence: The 2025 Global Natural History / Longitudinal Biofluid Study poster identifies AIIMS New Delhi and NIMHANS among participating institutions. Target ALS’s January 2026 update also describes tissue and genomic research resources.
limitations: Institutional involvement does not prove that a specific clinic is recruiting today or providing experimental treatment.
india_research.india_note: Confirm the exact protocol and recruitment status directly with the institution before arranging travel.

india_research.name: Treatment and trial access from India
india_research.subtitle: Approval · enrollment · personal import
india_research.summary: A treatment’s approval abroad, a company’s Indian presence and trial eligibility are separate questions.
india_research.evidence: CDSCO provides a personal-use import process: Form 12A is the application and Form 12B is the permit. Permission, prescription, product supply and clinical suitability require separate confirmation.
limitations: Import permission is not Indian marketing approval or evidence that a medicine works. This page does not certify current prices, reimbursement or supply.
india_research.india_note: Work with the treating team and licensed supply channels. Obtain written confirmation before committing to treatment-related travel or expense.
